endpoints.name: Support Search
endpoints.description: Free-text search across tickets, users, organizations and groups at once, using Zendesk's own query syntax. Rows of different kinds come back in one list, told apart by the result_type field. Reach for a specific resource's endpoint when the kind is already known -- this one is for when it is not.

endpoints.name: Support Users
endpoints.description: Everyone in the account, one row each: end users, agents and admins alike, told apart by the role field. Carries name, email, phone, role, active and suspended flags, locale, time_zone, tags, user_fields, organization_id, created_at and last_login_at. Use for agent rosters, customer counts, and joining tickets back to who raised or handled them.

endpoints: Help Desk Article Comments for User
Help Desk Post Comments for User
Help Desk User Segments for User

endpoints.name: Support Users for Group
endpoints.description: The agents in one group. Requires a group id.

endpoints: Help Desk Article Comments for User
Help Desk Post Comments for User
Help Desk User Segments for User

endpoints.name: Support Users for Organization
endpoints.description: The users belonging to one organization. Requires an organization id.

endpoints: Help Desk Article Comments for User
Help Desk Post Comments for User
Help Desk User Segments for User

endpoints.name: Support User
endpoints.description: A single user by its id. Same fields as Support Users.

endpoints.name: Support User Related Information
endpoints.description: Counts of what hangs off one user: assigned tickets, requested tickets, CC'd tickets, organization subscriptions. Requires a user id. A summary, not the tickets themselves.

endpoints.name: Support User Search
endpoints.description: Free-text search over users by name, email or external id. Returns the same shape as Support Users; use it when the identifier is known but the id is not.

endpoints.name: Support Deleted Users
endpoints.description: Users that have been deleted but not yet permanently purged. Carries the name and email they had, plus when they were deleted. Use for auditing removals.

endpoints.name: Support Deleted User
endpoints.description: A single deleted user by its id. Same fields as Support Deleted Users.

endpoints.name: Support Compliance Deletion Statuses
endpoints.description: The progress of GDPR-style deletion requests for one user, per brand. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Support Current User
endpoints.description: The user the API credentials belong to. One record, always the caller -- useful for verifying which account a connection is authenticated as.

endpoints.name: Support User Identities
endpoints.description: The verified contact points of one user -- email addresses, phone numbers, social handles -- with which is primary and whether each is verified. Requires a user id. Users carries only the primary email.

endpoints.name: Support User Identity
endpoints.description: A single identity of one user. Requires the user id as well.

endpoints.name: Support Password Requirements
endpoints.description: The password policy applying to one user. Configuration, not data.

endpoints.name: Support End User
endpoints.description: One end user by its id, restricted to the fields an end user is allowed to see about themselves. Support User returns the full record and is the usual choice.

endpoints.name: Support Groups
endpoints.description: The agent teams tickets are routed to, one row each. Carries name, description, whether the group is public, whether it is the account default, and created_at. Join tickets to it through group_id for per-team analysis.

endpoints.name: Support Groups for User
endpoints.description: The agent groups one user belongs to. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Support Assignable Groups
endpoints.description: Only the groups tickets can currently be assigned to. A subset of Support Groups, excluding deleted ones.

endpoints.name: Support Group
endpoints.description: A single group by its id. Same fields as Support Groups.

endpoints.name: Support Group Memberships
endpoints.description: Every agent-to-group link in the account, one row each, with which is that agent's default group. Use it to resolve the many-to-many between agents and groups in one pass.

endpoints.name: Support Group Memberships for User
endpoints.description: One user's group memberships as records, carrying which membership is the default. Requires a user id. Support Groups for User returns the groups themselves and is usually what is wanted.

endpoints.name: Support Group Memberships for Group
endpoints.description: The membership records of one group. Requires a group id.

endpoints.name: Support Assignable Memberships
endpoints.description: Only the group memberships that can take ticket assignments, account-wide.

endpoints.name: Support Assignable Memberships for Group
endpoints.description: The memberships of one group that can take ticket assignments. Requires a group id.

endpoints.name: Support Group Membership
endpoints.description: A single agent-to-group membership by its id, carrying whether it is that agent's default group.

endpoints.name: Support Group Membership for User
endpoints.description: A single group membership of one user. Requires the user id as well.

endpoints.name: Support Custom Roles
endpoints.description: The custom agent permission sets an account has defined, with what each is allowed to do. Configuration; join to Support Users through custom_role_id.

endpoints.name: Support Custom Role
endpoints.description: A single custom role by its id. Same fields as Support Custom Roles.

endpoints.name: Support Organizations
endpoints.description: The customer companies tickets and users are grouped under, one row each. Carries name, domain_names, tags, organization_fields, notes and details, whether tickets are shared within the organization, and created_at. Use for per-customer or per-account analysis; join tickets to it through organization_id.

endpoints.name: Support Organizations for User
endpoints.description: The organizations one user belongs to. Requires a user id. A user can belong to several.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Related Information
endpoints.description: Counts of what hangs off one organization: users, tickets and downgraded tickets. Requires an organization id.

endpoints.name: Support Organization
endpoints.description: A single organization by its id. Same fields as Support Organizations.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Subscriptions for Organization
endpoints.description: Who has subscribed to follow one organization's tickets. Requires an organization id.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Subscriptions
endpoints.description: Every organization-follow subscription in the account, one row each.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Subscriptions for User
endpoints.description: The organizations whose tickets one user has subscribed to follow. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Subscription
endpoints.description: A single organization subscription by its id.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Memberships
endpoints.description: Every user-to-organization link in the account, one row each, with which is that user's default. Use it to resolve the many-to-many between users and organizations in one pass rather than per user.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Memberships for User
endpoints.description: One user's organization memberships as records, carrying which is the default. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Memberships for Organization
endpoints.description: The membership records of one organization. Requires an organization id.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Membership
endpoints.description: A single organization membership by its id.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Membership for User
endpoints.description: A single organization membership of one user. Requires the user id as well.

endpoints.name: Support Requests
endpoints.description: The SAME underlying tickets as Support Tickets, seen from the end user's side. Carries subject, description, status, priority, organization and requester, but not the agent-only fields. Which one to use depends on whose view the question is about; for agent-side analysis Support Tickets is the fuller table.

endpoints.name: Support Open Requests
endpoints.description: Requests still open for the calling user. A scoped convenience list, not an account-wide open-ticket count -- for that, filter Support Tickets by status.

endpoints.name: Support Solved Requests
endpoints.description: Requests already solved for the calling user. Scoped to one person, like Support Open Requests.

endpoints.name: Support CCd Requests
endpoints.description: Requests the calling user is CC'd on rather than the requester of.

endpoints.name: Support Requests for User
endpoints.description: The requests raised by one user, end-user view. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Support Requests for Organization
endpoints.description: The requests belonging to one organization, end-user view. Requires an organization id.

endpoints.name: Support Request Search
endpoints.description: Free-text search across requests visible to the caller. Takes a query string; returns the same shape as Support Requests.

endpoints.name: Support Request
endpoints.description: A single request by its id. Same fields as Support Requests.

endpoints.name: Support Request Comments
endpoints.description: The conversation on one request, end-user side. Requires a request id. Public replies only -- internal notes are visible through Support Ticket Comments and not here.

endpoints.name: Support Request Comment
endpoints.description: A single comment on one request. Requires the request id as well.

endpoints.name: Support Tickets
endpoints.description: Support tickets, one row each -- the central table of a Zendesk account. Carries subject and description, status, priority, type, tags, custom_fields, created_at and updated_at, and the ids of requester, assignee, group, organization and brand. Use for ticket volume, backlog, and any breakdown by team, customer or category. Timing and SLA figures are NOT here: they live in Ticket Metrics.

endpoints: Support Routing Attribute Values for Ticket

endpoints.name: Support Tickets for Organization
endpoints.description: The tickets belonging to one organization. Requires an organization id. Equivalent to filtering Support Tickets by organization_id, and paged the same way.

endpoints: Support Routing Attribute Values for Ticket

endpoints.name: Support Requested Tickets for User
endpoints.description: The tickets one user raised. Requires a user id. Agent-side view, so fuller than Support Requests for User.

endpoints: Support Routing Attribute Values for Ticket

endpoints.name: Support CCd Tickets for User
endpoints.description: The tickets one user is CC'd on rather than assigned or requesting. Requires a user id.

endpoints: Support Routing Attribute Values for Ticket

endpoints.name: Support Assigned Tickets for User
endpoints.description: The tickets currently assigned to one agent. Requires a user id. Use for per-agent workload; for historical assignment, Support Ticket Audits records the changes.

endpoints: Support Routing Attribute Values for Ticket

endpoints.name: Support Recent Tickets
endpoints.description: The tickets the calling agent viewed most recently. A convenience list scoped to one person, not an account-wide feed -- of little use for analysis.

endpoints: Support Routing Attribute Values for Ticket

endpoints.name: Support Ticket
endpoints.description: A single ticket by its id. Same fields as Support Tickets; use it when the ticket id is already known rather than to scan or aggregate.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Related Information
endpoints.description: Counts of what hangs off one ticket: incidents, followups, topic and attachments. Requires a ticket id. A summary, not the linked records themselves.

endpoints.name: Support Deleted Tickets
endpoints.description: Tickets that have been deleted but not yet permanently purged, carrying the subject and requester they had and when they were removed. They are absent from Support Tickets, so a volume count taken there excludes them -- come here to see what was deleted.

endpoints: Support Routing Attribute Values for Ticket

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Collaborators
endpoints.description: The users CC'd on one ticket. Requires a ticket id. Use for who else was looped in.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Followers
endpoints.description: The agents following one ticket without being assigned to it. Requires a ticket id.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Email CCs
endpoints.description: The users receiving email copies of one ticket. Requires a ticket id.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Incidents
endpoints.description: The incident tickets linked to one problem ticket. Requires a problem ticket id. Use for how many customers were hit by the same underlying issue.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Problems
endpoints.description: Only the tickets of type 'problem', the ones other tickets are linked to as incidents. Use it to find the underlying issues that generated the most incidents; the incidents themselves are reachable per problem through Support Ticket Incidents.

endpoints.name: Support Attachment
endpoints.description: A single file attached to a ticket comment, by its id. Carries file name, size, content type, and the thumbnails generated for it.

endpoints.name: Support Satisfaction Ratings
endpoints.description: Customer satisfaction responses, one row per rating. Carries the score (good or bad), the free-text comment, reason and reason_code for a bad rating, created_at, and the ids of the ticket, requester, assignee and group. The table for CSAT, and for which agents or teams the ratings attach to.

endpoints.name: Support Satisfaction Rating
endpoints.description: A single satisfaction rating by its id. Same fields as Support Satisfaction Ratings.

endpoints.name: Support Satisfaction Reasons
endpoints.description: The account's list of reasons a customer can pick when giving a bad rating, with the id and text of each. This is the KEY to the reason_code column on Support Satisfaction Ratings, which stores only a numeric code -- without joining this table, bad-rating analysis can count the ratings but cannot say why.

endpoints.name: Support Satisfaction Reason
endpoints.description: A single satisfaction reason by its id. Same fields as Support Satisfaction Reasons.

endpoints.name: Support Suspended Tickets
endpoints.description: Inbound messages held back as suspected spam or from unrecognised senders, before they ever became tickets. Carries the author, subject, cause of suspension, and when it will be purged. They are NOT in Support Tickets -- use this to see what was filtered out.

endpoints.name: Support Suspended Ticket
endpoints.description: A single suspended ticket by its id. Same fields as Support Suspended Tickets.

endpoints: Support Routing Attribute Values for Ticket

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Audits
endpoints.description: Every change made to every ticket, account-wide. The complete change log -- large, and paged from the beginning of the account. Prefer the per-ticket audits unless a full history is genuinely needed.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Audits for Ticket
endpoints.description: Every change ever made to one ticket, with who changed what and when. Requires a ticket id. Use for auditing a single ticket's history.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Audit
endpoints.description: A single audit record of one ticket. Requires the ticket id as well.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Comments
endpoints.description: The conversation on one ticket: every public reply and internal note, with author, body, whether it is public, and attachments. Requires a ticket id. This is where the text of a conversation lives -- Tickets carries only the opening description.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Skips
endpoints.description: Every ticket an agent skipped in guided mode, account-wide, with the reason given. Use for reviewing how queues are being worked through; the per-agent and per-ticket views are separate endpoints.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Skips for Ticket
endpoints.description: Records of agents skipping over one ticket in guided mode, with the reason given. Requires a ticket id.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Skips for User
endpoints.description: Tickets one agent skipped in guided mode, with the reason. Requires a user id. Use for reviewing how an agent works through a queue.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Metrics
endpoints.description: Timing and effort measurements per ticket, one row each -- the table SLA and responsiveness questions actually need. Carries first_resolution_time_in_minutes and full_resolution_time_in_minutes, reply_time_in_minutes, agent_wait_time and requester_wait_time, on_hold_time, the number of replies and reopens, and assignee and group station counts. Tickets itself has none of this.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Metric
endpoints.description: The timing measurements of one ticket, by the metric id. Same fields as Support Ticket Metrics.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Metrics for Ticket
endpoints.description: The timing measurements of one ticket. Requires a ticket id. Same fields as Support Ticket Metrics.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Activities
endpoints.description: The activity feed of what happened recently on tickets the calling agent is involved with -- assignments, comments, status changes. Scoped to the caller rather than the account, so it is not a general audit trail; Support Ticket Audits is.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Activity
endpoints.description: A single activity record by its id. Same fields as Support Ticket Activities.

endpoints.name: Support Sessions
endpoints.description: Every active login session in the account, with the user, when it began and when it was last used. Account-wide, unlike the per-user sessions endpoint. Use for security review.

endpoints.name: Support Sessions for User
endpoints.description: The active login sessions of one user, with when each was created and last used. Requires a user id. Use for security review.

endpoints.name: Support Session
endpoints.description: A single session of one user. Requires the user id as well.

endpoints.name: Support Current Session
endpoints.description: The session the API credentials are using. One record, always the caller's.

endpoints.name: Support Most Popular Tags
endpoints.description: The account's tags ranked by how often they are used, with a count for each. A ready-made frequency table -- cheaper than aggregating the tags column across tickets, and the usual answer to what customers write in about.

endpoints.name: Support Tags for Ticket
endpoints.description: The tags on one ticket. Requires a ticket id.

endpoints.name: Support Tags for Organization
endpoints.description: The tags on one organization. Requires an organization id.

endpoints.name: Support Tags for User
endpoints.description: The tags on one user. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Support Views
endpoints.description: The saved ticket filters agents work from, one row each. Carries the view's title, whether it is active and who it is shared with, plus the conditions that define it. This is the definition of a view, not its contents -- the tickets it matches come from Support View Tickets.

endpoints.name: Support View
endpoints.description: A single view by its id. Same fields as Support Views.

endpoints.name: Support View Tickets
endpoints.description: The tickets currently matching one view. Requires a view id. Returns ticket rows, so it is a pre-filtered slice of Support Tickets -- useful when a question is framed in terms of a queue the team already uses.

endpoints: Support Routing Attribute Values for Ticket

endpoints.name: Support View Counts
endpoints.description: How many tickets each of several views currently matches, for the view ids given. Cheap compared with fetching the tickets, so it suits backlog-size questions across queues.

endpoints.name: Support View Count
endpoints.description: How many tickets one view currently matches. Requires a view id.

endpoints.name: Support View Search
endpoints.description: Finds views by title. Returns the same shape as Support Views; use it when the view is known by name rather than by id.

endpoints.name: Support Triggers
endpoints.description: The rules that fire the moment a ticket is created or updated, each with its conditions, the actions it performs, whether it is active, and its position in the run order. WORTH READING BEFORE INTERPRETING TICKET DATA: triggers set priority, assign groups, add tags and send notifications automatically, so a great many field values on a ticket were put there by a rule rather than by a person. Position matters -- triggers run in order and a later one can overwrite an earlier one's work, which is why the same conditions can produce different outcomes.

endpoints.name: Support Trigger
endpoints.description: One trigger by id, with its full condition and action set.

endpoints.name: Support Active Triggers
endpoints.description: Only the triggers currently switched on. A subset of Support Triggers, and the one that reflects what is actually happening to tickets now -- inactive rules remain in the full list and explain nothing about current behaviour.

endpoints.name: Support Trigger Search
endpoints.description: Triggers matching a search term across name and description. Use it to find the rule responsible for a behaviour when its name is only half remembered.

endpoints.name: Support Trigger Definitions
endpoints.description: The conditions and actions a trigger may be built from, as reference data. The vocabulary rules are written in -- useful for interpreting a condition whose field name means nothing on its own.

endpoints.name: Support Trigger Revisions
endpoints.description: The CHANGE HISTORY of one trigger: each past version with who saved it and when. Requires a trigger id. Genuinely an audit trail rather than configuration -- when ticket behaviour changed on a particular date and nobody remembers why, this is where the answer is, and no ticket table records it.

endpoints.name: Support Trigger Revision
endpoints.description: One past version of a trigger, with its conditions and actions as they stood. Requires the trigger id and revision id. Use it to see exactly what a rule did during a period being analysed.

endpoints.name: Support Automations
endpoints.description: The rules that fire on ELAPSED TIME rather than on an event -- escalate after four hours, close after seven days, notify when an SLA is about to breach. Each carries conditions, actions and whether it is active. The distinction from triggers matters: automations run hourly against every open ticket, so status changes and escalations that appear to have no actor behind them usually came from here.

endpoints.name: Support Automation
endpoints.description: One automation by id, with its conditions and actions.

endpoints.name: Support Active Automations
endpoints.description: Only the automations currently switched on.

endpoints.name: Support Automation Search
endpoints.description: Automations matching a search term.

endpoints.name: Support SLA Policies
endpoints.description: The service level agreements the account applies: which tickets each covers, and the targets it sets for first reply, next reply and resolution, per priority. The measurements in Support Ticket Metrics are only meaningful against these -- a resolution time is fast or slow relative to the target set here.

endpoints.name: Support SLA Policy
endpoints.description: A single SLA policy by its id. Same fields as Support SLA Policies.

endpoints.name: Support SLA Policy Definitions
endpoints.description: The filter conditions and target types an SLA policy may be built from. Reference data for interpreting or constructing policies, not the policies themselves.

endpoints.name: Support Targets
endpoints.description: The external destinations Zendesk can notify when a rule fires -- an HTTP endpoint, an email address, or a third-party service. Configuration; the notifications themselves are not recorded here, but their FAILURES are, in Support Target Failures.

endpoints.name: Support Target
endpoints.description: One target by id, with its type and destination.

endpoints.name: Support Target Failures
endpoints.description: The notifications to external targets that FAILED, with the target, the response received, and when it happened. NOT configuration -- this is operational data, and the only place a silently broken integration shows up: a rule that fires correctly into a dead endpoint leaves no mark on any ticket, and this table is the mark.

endpoints.name: Support Target Failure
endpoints.description: One target failure by id, with the full request and response bodies. The detail behind a failure, and where the actual payload is visible.

endpoints.name: Support Macros
endpoints.description: The bulk actions agents apply to tickets by hand -- set status, add a canned reply, change assignee, all in one click. Each carries its actions, whether it is active, and its restriction. Macros are the closest thing to a record of standard practice: which are used and which are not says a good deal about how a team actually works, though the usage counts themselves are not in this connector.

endpoints.name: Support Macro
endpoints.description: One macro by id, with its full action set.

endpoints.name: Support Active Macros
endpoints.description: Only the macros currently available. A subset of Support Macros.

endpoints.name: Support Macro Categories
endpoints.description: The categories macros are filed under, as a plain list of names. Organisational grouping.

endpoints.name: Support Macro Search
endpoints.description: Macros matching a search term.

endpoints.name: Support Macro Actions
endpoints.description: The actions across all macros. Use it to find every macro that sets a particular field or applies a particular tag -- which the per-macro records cannot answer without reading each one.

endpoints.name: Support Macro Action Definitions
endpoints.description: The actions a macro may be built from, as reference data.

endpoints.name: Support Macro Attachments
endpoints.description: The files attached to one macro, so that applying it also attaches them. Requires a macro id.

endpoints.name: Support Macro Attachment
endpoints.description: One macro attachment by id.

endpoints.name: Support Brands
endpoints.description: The brands a multi-brand account serves, one row each. Carries name, subdomain, host mapping, logo and whether the brand is active and the default. Tickets carry a brand_id, so this is the dimension for splitting any ticket analysis by brand.

lookups.endpoint: Support Host Mapping Validity for Brand

endpoints.name: Support Brand
endpoints.description: A single brand by its id. Same fields as Support Brands.

endpoints.name: Support Host Mapping Validity
endpoints.description: Checks whether a proposed host mapping resolves correctly in DNS. A validation call rather than a data endpoint -- it reports on a hostname supplied to it, not on anything stored.

endpoints.name: Support Host Mapping Validity for Brand
endpoints.description: The same DNS check for one existing brand. Requires a brand id. Use it to find a brand whose custom domain has stopped resolving, which would otherwise surface only as customers unable to reach the help centre.

endpoints.name: Support Dynamic Content Items
endpoints.description: The reusable text snippets used in macros, triggers and automations, each with a default locale and a placeholder name. Content rather than configuration: the words customers actually receive live here rather than in the rules that send them, so the text of an automated reply is only readable through this table.

endpoints.name: Support Dynamic Content Item
endpoints.description: One dynamic content item by id, with its variants.

endpoints.name: Support Dynamic Content Variants
endpoints.description: The per-locale translations of one item, each with its locale, its text, and whether it is the default and whether it is active. Requires an item id. A multilingual account keeps its real customer-facing wording here, one row per language.

endpoints.name: Support Dynamic Content Variant
endpoints.description: One variant by id. Requires the item id as well.

endpoints.name: Support Locales
endpoints.description: The locales the account has enabled, with the id, code and name of each. Needed to interpret the locale_id carried on users and tickets.

endpoints.name: Support Public Locales
endpoints.description: Only the locales available to end users, a subset of Support Locales.

endpoints.name: Support Agent Locales
endpoints.description: Only the locales agents may use for the admin interface.

endpoints.name: Support Locale
endpoints.description: A single locale by its id. Same fields as Support Locales.

endpoints.name: Support Current Locale
endpoints.description: The locale of the calling user. One record, always the caller's.

endpoints.name: Support Schedules
endpoints.description: The business hours the account runs on, with the working intervals of each schedule and its time zone. SLA clocks and wait-time metrics count business hours rather than wall-clock time where a schedule applies, so a resolution time cannot be read correctly without knowing which schedule was in force.

endpoints.name: Support Schedule
endpoints.description: A single schedule by its id. Same fields as Support Schedules.

endpoints.name: Support Schedule Holidays
endpoints.description: The dates one schedule treats as non-working. Requires a schedule id. Part of the same business-hours calculation as the schedule itself.

endpoints.name: Support Schedule Holiday
endpoints.description: A single holiday of one schedule. Requires the schedule id as well.

endpoints.name: Support Sharing Agreements
endpoints.description: The agreements to share tickets with other Zendesk accounts, with the partner, the direction and the status. Genuinely worth knowing when reconciling counts: tickets shared in from a partner appear in this account, and tickets shared out are worked on elsewhere, so a volume figure can include or exclude work the team never touched.

endpoints.name: Support Sharing Agreement
endpoints.description: One sharing agreement by id.

endpoints.name: Support Addresses
endpoints.description: The support email addresses the account receives on, with the address, the brand it belongs to, its default flag, and its forwarding and DNS verification status. Inbound mail arrives through these, so this is what maps an incoming ticket to a brand or a product line -- and the verification status is why mail to a given address may not be arriving at all.

endpoints.name: Support Address
endpoints.description: One recipient address by id, with its verification status.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Forms
endpoints.description: The alternative ticket layouts an account offers, each exposing a different set of fields. Carries name, whether it is active and whether end users see it. Configuration -- use it to interpret which custom fields apply to which tickets.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Form
endpoints.description: A single ticket form by its id. Same fields as Support Ticket Forms.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a ticket can carry, standard and custom. Carries the field type, title, whether it is required and active, and the position. This is the KEY to custom_fields on Support Tickets, which stores only numeric field ids and raw values -- without this table those columns cannot be read.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Field
endpoints.description: A single ticket field by its id. Same fields as Support Ticket Fields.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Field Options
endpoints.description: The permitted values of one dropdown ticket field, with the stored value and its display name. Requires a field id. Needed to turn a stored option value into something readable.

endpoints.name: Support Ticket Field Option
endpoints.description: A single option of one ticket field. Requires the field id as well.

endpoints.name: Support User Fields
endpoints.description: Every custom field defined on users, standard ones excluded. Carries the field key, type, title, whether it is active, and its position. This is the KEY to the user_fields column on Support Users, which stores values against these keys -- those values cannot be interpreted without it.

endpoints.name: Support User Field
endpoints.description: A single user field by its id. Same fields as Support User Fields.

endpoints.name: Support User Field Options
endpoints.description: The permitted values of one dropdown user field, with the stored value and its display name. Requires a field id.

endpoints.name: Support User Field Option
endpoints.description: A single option of one user field. Requires the field id as well.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Fields
endpoints.description: Every custom field defined on organizations. Carries the field key, type, title and whether it is active. The KEY to the organization_fields column on Support Organizations, in the same way user fields are for users.

endpoints.name: Support Organization Field
endpoints.description: A single organization field by its id. Same fields as Support Organization Fields.

endpoints.name: Support Job Statuses
endpoints.description: The state of asynchronous bulk operations -- bulk updates, imports, deletions -- with progress, results, and any errors per item. Use it to check whether a bulk change actually completed; the operation reports only that it was queued.

endpoints.name: Support Job Status
endpoints.description: A single job status by its id. Same fields as Support Job Statuses.

endpoints.name: Support Routing Attributes
endpoints.description: The skills defined for skills-based routing -- language, product, tier -- each with a name. Requires the skills-based routing feature. The definitions; which agents hold them and which tickets need them are separate tables.

endpoints.name: Support Routing Attribute
endpoints.description: One routing attribute by id.

endpoints.name: Support Routing Attribute Definitions
endpoints.description: The conditions skill routing rules may be built from, as reference data.

endpoints.name: Support Routing Attribute Values
endpoints.description: The possible values of one attribute -- the individual skills within a category, such as the languages under Language. Requires an attribute id. THE KEY to the skill assignments: agent and ticket records reference these values by id.

endpoints.name: Support Routing Attribute Value
endpoints.description: One attribute value by id. Requires the attribute id as well.

endpoints.name: Support Routing Attribute Values for Ticket
endpoints.description: The skills one ticket requires. Requires a ticket id. Paired with the agent skills, this is what determined who the ticket could be routed to.

endpoints.name: Support Routing Attribute Values for Agent
endpoints.description: The skills one agent actually holds. Requires a user id. Data rather than configuration -- it is the answer to who can handle what, and the constraint that explains why a ticket sat unassigned while agents were free.

endpoints.name: Support Tickets Fulfilled by Current User
endpoints.description: The tickets whose skill requirements the calling agent satisfies. Scoped to the caller, so it describes one person's eligible queue rather than the account's routing state.

endpoints.name: Support Workspaces
endpoints.description: The agent workspaces configured -- named combinations of ticket form, macros and apps that appear together for particular kinds of work. Requires the feature to be enabled. Configuration of the agent interface; it shapes how tickets are handled but records nothing about any ticket.

endpoints.name: Support Workspace
endpoints.description: One workspace by id.

endpoints.name: Support Apps
endpoints.description: The Zendesk apps available to the account, with name, author, state and the settings each defines. Apps extend the agent interface and frequently write their own data into ticket fields or custom objects, so an unexplained field on a ticket is often an app's doing -- which makes this list worth checking before concluding a column has no source.

endpoints.name: Support App
endpoints.description: One app by id, with its full settings definition.

endpoints.name: Support Owned Apps
endpoints.description: Only the apps this account authored, as opposed to those installed from the marketplace.

endpoints.name: Support App Installations
endpoints.description: The apps actually INSTALLED, with their configured settings and whether each is enabled. The distinction from Support Apps matters: that lists what is available, this lists what is running, and only the second explains current behaviour.

endpoints.name: Support App Installation
endpoints.description: One app installation by id, with its settings as configured on this account.

endpoints.name: Support App Installation Status
endpoints.description: The progress of an app installation job. Operational, and short-lived.

endpoints.name: Support App Requirements
endpoints.description: The Zendesk objects an installed app created for itself -- custom ticket fields, targets, triggers and the like. Requires an installation id. THE ANSWER TO WHERE AN UNEXPLAINED FIELD CAME FROM: objects listed here were created by the app rather than by an administrator, and removing the app removes them.

endpoints.name: Support App Location Installations
endpoints.description: Which apps occupy which interface locations, and in what order. Interface configuration.

endpoints.name: Support App Locations
endpoints.description: The places in the interface an app can appear -- ticket sidebar, top bar, modal. Reference data, identical on every account.

endpoints.name: Support App Location
endpoints.description: One app location by id.

endpoints.name: Support OAuth Clients
endpoints.description: The OAuth applications registered against the account, each with its name, identifier and redirect URLs. Integration and security inventory -- these are the applications permitted to act on the account's behalf, and they hold access that appears in no user or agent list.

endpoints.name: Support OAuth Clients for Current User
endpoints.description: The OAuth applications registered by the calling user. Integration configuration, not ticket data.

endpoints.name: Support OAuth Client
endpoints.description: One OAuth client by id.

endpoints.name: Support OAuth Tokens
endpoints.description: The ACTIVE access tokens issued, with the client they belong to, the scopes granted, and when each was created and last used. Security audit material rather than configuration: a token nobody recognises, or one with broad scopes and no recent use, is exactly what an access review looks for.

endpoints.name: Support OAuth Token
endpoints.description: One OAuth token by id, with its scopes.

endpoints.name: Support OAuth Current Token
endpoints.description: The token the current request is authenticated with, and its scopes. One record, always the caller's -- and the quickest explanation for a permission error, since the scopes here decide what the rest of this connector can reach.

endpoints.name: Support Authorized Global Clients
endpoints.description: The globally registered Zendesk applications this account has authorised. Third-party access granted at the marketplace level rather than by the account itself.

endpoints.name: Support Account Settings
endpoints.description: Every account-level setting in one record -- which channels are enabled, whether satisfaction ratings are collected, whether voting and following are on, the ticket and branding options, and the active feature set. READ THIS FIRST WHEN A TABLE COMES BACK EMPTY. Several endpoints in this connector return nothing not because there is no data but because the feature behind them is switched off, and this is the only place that distinction is visible: satisfaction ratings absent because CSAT was never enabled looks identical to satisfaction ratings absent because nobody responded.

endpoints.name: Support Audit Logs
endpoints.description: Administrative changes to the account itself: settings altered, users created or deactivated, roles changed -- who did what and when. Distinct from Support Ticket Audits, which records changes to tickets. Use for compliance and change review.

endpoints.name: Support Audit Log
endpoints.description: A single audit log entry by its id. Same fields as Support Audit Logs.

endpoints.name: Support Bookmarks
endpoints.description: The tickets the calling agent has bookmarked. Always the caller's own, so it is a personal shortlist rather than any measure of the account.

endpoints.name: Support Resource Collections
endpoints.description: Bundles of Zendesk objects created together by an app or an installation, tracked as a unit so they can be removed together. Housekeeping metadata; the objects themselves live in their own tables.

endpoints.name: Support Resource Collection
endpoints.description: One resource collection by id, with the objects it groups.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Articles
endpoints.description: The knowledge base articles themselves, one row each -- the content agents publish for customers to read. Carries title, body, locale, author_id, section_id, created_at and updated_at, draft and promoted flags, position, outdated, and the running vote_sum, vote_count and comments_count. The table for knowledge base questions: how many articles exist, which are most or least useful, what is stale.

endpoints: Help Desk Article Labels for Article
Help Desk Missing Translations for Article
Help Desk Votes for Article Comment

endpoints.name: Help Desk Articles for Category
endpoints.description: The articles in one category, across all of its sections. Requires a category id.

endpoints: Help Desk Article Labels for Article
Help Desk Missing Translations for Article
Help Desk Votes for Article Comment

endpoints.name: Help Desk Articles for Section
endpoints.description: The articles in one section. Requires a section id.

endpoints: Help Desk Article Labels for Article
Help Desk Missing Translations for Article
Help Desk Votes for Article Comment

endpoints.name: Help Desk Articles for User
endpoints.description: The articles written by one user. Requires a user id. Use for per-author output.

endpoints: Help Desk Article Labels for Article
Help Desk Missing Translations for Article
Help Desk Votes for Article Comment

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article
endpoints.description: A single article by its id. Same fields as Help Desk Articles.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Attachments
endpoints.description: The files attached to one article. Requires an article id. Carries the file name, size, content type and whether it is inline.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Inline Attachments
endpoints.description: Only the attachments embedded in one article's body, as opposed to listed beside it. Requires an article id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Block Attachments
endpoints.description: Only the attachments listed as separate downloads on one article, as opposed to embedded in the body. Requires an article id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Attachment
endpoints.description: A single article attachment by its id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Comments
endpoints.description: Reader comments left on articles, one row each. Carries the body, author_id, the article it belongs to, created_at, and its own vote_sum and vote_count. Use for which articles provoke discussion, and as feedback text alongside the numeric votes.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Comments for User
endpoints.description: The article comments written by one user. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Comment
endpoints.description: A single article comment. Requires the article id as well.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Labels
endpoints.description: Every label defined across the knowledge base, one row each. Labels are free-form tags on articles; use them to slice article analysis by topic when sections are too coarse.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Label
endpoints.description: A single label by its id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Labels for Article
endpoints.description: The labels attached to one article. Requires an article id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Categories
endpoints.description: The top level of the knowledge base. Categories hold sections, and sections hold articles -- this is the outermost of those three. Carries name, description, position, locale and whether it is visible to end users. Use it to give article analysis a top-level dimension.

endpoints: Help Desk Missing Translations for Category

endpoints.name: Help Desk Category
endpoints.description: A single category by its id. Same fields as Help Desk Categories.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Permission Groups
endpoints.description: The groups controlling who may create and edit knowledge base content, with each group's name and membership. Guide's authoring permissions, and therefore the explanation for who could have written or changed an article -- the article itself records only its author.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Permission Group
endpoints.description: One permission group by id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Search
endpoints.description: Full-text search across article titles and bodies, using Help Center's own query syntax. Returns the same shape as Help Desk Articles, ranked by relevance.
endpoints.suffix: /api/v2/help_center/articles/search.json?query={Query}&category={Category ID?}&section={Section ID?}&label_names={Labels?}&locale={Locale?}&multibrand={Multibrand?:true|false}&brand_id={Brand ID?}&created_before={Created Before?:YYYY-MM-DD}&created_after={Created After?:YYYY-MM-DD}&created_at={Created On?:YYYY-MM-DD}&updated_before={Updated Before?:YYYY-MM-DD}&updated_after={Updated After?:YYYY-MM-DD}&updated_at={Updated On?:YYYY-MM-DD}

endpoints.name: Help Desk Post Search
endpoints.description: Full-text search across community posts. Returns the same shape as Help Desk Posts, ranked by relevance.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Translations for Article
endpoints.description: The localized versions of one article, one row per locale. Carries title, body, locale, whether that translation is the source, and its own created_at and updated_at. Requires an article id. Multilingual knowledge bases hold their real text here rather than on the article.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Translations for Section
endpoints.description: The localized versions of one section's name and description. Requires a section id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Translations for Category
endpoints.description: The localized versions of one category's name and description. Requires a category id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Missing Translations for Article
endpoints.description: The locales one article has NOT been translated into. Requires an article id. Use for localization coverage gaps -- it answers what is absent, which the translations list cannot.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Missing Translations for Section
endpoints.description: The locales one section has not been translated into. Requires a section id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Missing Translations for Category
endpoints.description: The locales one category has not been translated into. Requires a category id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Translation
endpoints.description: A single translation by its id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Locales
endpoints.description: The locales the Help Center is configured for, and which is the default. Needed to interpret the locale column on articles and translations.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Themes
endpoints.description: The Guide themes installed for the help centre, with name, version, author and which is live. Presentation of the customer-facing knowledge base; it affects nothing in the content tables.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Theme
endpoints.description: One theme by id, with its settings and assets.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Theming Job
endpoints.description: The progress of a theme import or update job. Operational and short-lived.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Topics
endpoints.description: The top level of the community forum: the areas users post in. Carries name, description, position, and the running follower_count. Community content is user-written, unlike the knowledge base articles which staff publish -- the two are separate bodies of content that happen to share this API.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Topic
endpoints.description: A single community topic by its id. Same fields as Help Desk Topics.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Posts
endpoints.description: The community posts users write, one row each. Carries title, details, author_id, the parent topic_id, status, pinned and closed flags, created_at, and the running vote_sum, vote_count, comment_count and follower_count. The table for community activity: what is being asked, what draws responses, what is unanswered.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Posts for Topic
endpoints.description: The posts in one topic. Requires a topic id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Posts for User
endpoints.description: The posts written by one user. Requires a user id. Use for per-contributor activity.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Post
endpoints.description: A single post by its id. Same fields as Help Desk Posts.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Post Comments
endpoints.description: The replies on one post, one row each. Carries the body, author_id, created_at, its own votes, and whether it is marked as the official answer. Requires a post id. Use for response rates and for which answers were accepted.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Post Comments for User
endpoints.description: The community replies written by one user. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Post Comment
endpoints.description: A single post comment. Requires the post id as well.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Sections
endpoints.description: The middle level of the knowledge base: groupings of articles inside a category. Carries name, description, position, locale, the parent category_id and visibility. Join articles to it through section_id.

endpoints: Help Desk Missing Translations for Section

endpoints.name: Help Desk Sections for Category
endpoints.description: The sections inside one category. Requires a category id.

endpoints: Help Desk Missing Translations for Section

endpoints.name: Help Desk Section
endpoints.description: A single section by its id. Same fields as Help Desk Sections.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Subscriptions
endpoints.description: Who has subscribed to be notified about one article. Requires an article id. Use as an interest signal per article.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Article Subscription
endpoints.description: A single article subscription. Requires the article id as well.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Section Subscriptions
endpoints.description: Who has subscribed to one section, and so to everything published in it. Requires a section id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Section Subscription
endpoints.description: A single section subscription. Requires the section id as well.

endpoints.name: Help Desk User Subscriptions
endpoints.description: Everything one user has subscribed to, across articles, sections, posts and topics. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Post Subscriptions
endpoints.description: Who is following one post. Requires a post id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Post Subscription
endpoints.description: A single post subscription. Requires the post id as well.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Topic Subscriptions
endpoints.description: Who is following one topic, and so everything posted in it. Requires a topic id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Topic Subscription
endpoints.description: A single topic subscription. Requires the topic id as well.

endpoints.name: Help Desk User Segments
endpoints.description: The audience rules that decide who can see which content -- by tag, organization or role. Configuration rather than content, but needed to explain why an article is visible to some readers and not others.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Applicable User Segments
endpoints.description: The segments the calling user falls into. Scoped to the caller, not an account-wide list.

endpoints.name: Help Desk User Segments for User
endpoints.description: The segments one user falls into. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk User Segment
endpoints.description: A single user segment by its id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk User Segment Sections
endpoints.description: The sections one segment grants access to. Requires a segment id.

endpoints: Help Desk Missing Translations for Section

endpoints.name: Help Desk User Segment Topics
endpoints.description: The community topics one segment grants access to. Requires a segment id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Votes for User
endpoints.description: Every vote one user has cast, across articles, posts and comments alike. Requires a user id. Use for reader engagement per person.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Votes for Article
endpoints.description: The individual up and down votes cast on one article, each carrying its value and who cast it. Requires an article id. Articles already carries the totals as vote_sum and vote_count -- come here only when the individual votes or the voters matter.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Votes for Article Comment
endpoints.description: The individual votes cast on one article comment. Requires the comment id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Votes for Post
endpoints.description: The individual votes cast on one community post. Requires a post id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Votes for Post Comment
endpoints.description: The individual votes cast on one community post comment. Requires the comment id.

endpoints.name: Help Desk Vote
endpoints.description: A single vote by its id, carrying its value and the item it was cast on.

endpoints.name: Talk Phone Number Search
endpoints.description: Available numbers to purchase, by country and pattern. A procurement lookup against Zendesk's inventory rather than anything the account holds.

endpoints.name: Talk Phone Numbers
endpoints.description: The phone numbers the account owns, each with its number, country, capabilities (voice, SMS, MMS), the brand and group it routes to, whether recording and voicemail are enabled, and its monthly price. Not purely configuration: the price column makes this the voice channel's cost table, and the routing columns explain which team a call reached.

endpoints.name: Talk Phone Number
endpoints.description: One phone number by id, with its routing and recording settings.

endpoints.name: Talk Availability
endpoints.description: One agent's voice availability -- whether they are accepting calls, and their status. Requires a user id. A live snapshot rather than a history, so it answers who is available now and cannot describe any past period.

endpoints.name: Talk Greeting Categories
endpoints.description: The kinds of greeting a recording can be -- voicemail, hold, wait, and so on. Reference data, fixed by Zendesk.

endpoints.name: Talk Greeting Category
endpoints.description: One greeting category by id.

endpoints.name: Talk Greetings
endpoints.description: The recorded greetings the account uses, each with its category, name, and which numbers it is assigned to. Configuration of what callers hear.

endpoints.name: Talk Greeting
endpoints.description: One greeting by id.

endpoints.name: Talk Current Queue Activity
endpoints.description: A live snapshot of the call queue right now -- how many calls are waiting, the longest wait, and how many agents are online. Real-time state, not history: it answers what is happening at this instant and cannot be used for trends.

endpoints.name: Talk Account Overview
endpoints.description: Account-wide voice metrics for Zendesk Talk: call volume, average wait and talk time, abandonment, voicemail counts and service levels. One aggregate record rather than a list. The starting point for phone-channel questions -- Support Tickets holds the tickets calls created, not the call statistics themselves.

endpoints.name: Talk Agents Overview
endpoints.description: The same voice metrics broken down per agent: calls handled, average talk time, wait time and availability. Use for phone-channel workload and responsiveness by person.

endpoints.name: Talk Agents Activity Statistics
endpoints.description: Per-agent activity in Talk over time, one row per agent: how long they spent available, on calls, and wrapping up. Use for utilisation and staffing questions.

endpoints.name: Talk Addresses
endpoints.description: The physical addresses registered for voice numbers, held for regulatory compliance. Many countries require a verified local address before a number can be bought or kept, so this is what explains a number that cannot be provisioned.

endpoints.name: Talk Address
endpoints.description: One voice address by id.

endpoints.name: Talk Interactive Voice Responses
endpoints.description: The IVR phone menus configured -- the 'press one for sales' trees. Each carries its name and the phone numbers it answers. The structure here decides which queue a caller lands in, so it is the explanation for how call volume is distributed across groups; the calls themselves are in the Talk statistics endpoints.

endpoints.name: Talk Interactive Voice Response
endpoints.description: One IVR by id, with its menus.

endpoints.name: Talk Interactive Voice Response Menus
endpoints.description: The menus within one IVR, including which is the greeting menu. Requires an IVR id. A menu is one level of the tree.

endpoints.name: Talk Interactive Voice Response Menu
endpoints.description: One IVR menu by id. Requires the IVR id as well.

endpoints.name: Talk Interactive Voice Response Routes
endpoints.description: The options within one menu -- which keypress leads where, whether to a group, another menu or voicemail. Requires the IVR and menu ids. THE ACTUAL ROUTING RULES: this is the level at which a caller's choice becomes a destination, and therefore where a misrouted queue is diagnosed.

endpoints.name: Talk Interactive Voice Response Route
endpoints.description: One IVR route by id, with its keypress and destination.
